clusters.name: Connector-held secrets delivered into browser pages (connector-to-browser credential bridge)
clusters.description: A connected account (mailbox, vault, credential broker) supplies a secret such as an email one-time code or a login credential directly into a page the agent is driving, after user approval, without the model ever seeing the value.

bestInClass.why: q5 SRC: strict preconditions (https origin, frame origin equals page origin, exactly one non-password prompt field, bound conversation), explicit user elicitation saying the model cannot see the code, native delivery path; secrets come from a local broker socket with versioned bindings rather than through model context.

clusters.mechanism: Model calls browserAuth.request(otpHandle) on a tab. Runtime checks: origin https; frame origin == top origin; exactly one required non-password input; no options/QR; credential-observation gate on; conversation id bound; otherwise returns status 'unavailable'. It then raises a user elicitation (kind browser_email_otp, requires user input, not auto-approvable by a guardian). On approval the host (not the model runtime) fetches the code from the mail connector via a broker socket (BROWSER_AUTH_BROKER_SOCKET_PATH, credential binding version 1|2) and types it through a native input path; the model receives only a status. Re-implementation: Model Plane emits a fill_secret proposal {target elementRef, secretRef vault://connection/<id>/<kind>}; the Quarry executor validates origin/field preconditions and a BrowserBroker sensitive child grant, calls integration-corev2 /internal/connectors/token (or a new OTP-fetch op) over service auth, fills via CDP Input.insertText, and redacts the value from observations, receipts and artifacts.

evidence: apps/Ingestion Plane/integration-corev2/internal/egress/guard.go:23 (only Quarry mention in IC, a comment)
apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/QUARRY_V2_BROWSER_AUTOMATION_IMPROVEMENTS_2026_OWNERSHIP_RECONCILED.md:1106-1127 (DOC plan: fill_secret with vault:// secretRef resolved at the executor boundary)
verevon.gap: Code-absent: no code path lets a Quarry browser run use a connector token, mailbox OTP or vault secret; authenticated web access is either OAuth API actions (integration-corev2) or browser cookies (Quarry profiles) and the two never meet. Only a DOC plan (section 19.1 secret references) exists. Missing: a secretRef action type in Quarry contracts, executor-side resolution via the IC token broker, origin/field preconditions, a sensitive-grant scope, redaction of the filled value from observations/receipts, and the user elicitation UI.
verevon.strengths: Building blocks exist: AES-GCM token vault and internal token broker in IC, BrowserBroker sensitive single-use child grants, Model-proposes/Quarry-executes contract.

clusters.benefit: Lets agents complete logins and email-verification steps on sites without API connectors while keeping secrets out of model context. This is the core promise of a governed AI browser and the main place where IC and Quarry should meet. Fits the authority model: Model proposes, Quarry executes, IC holds secrets.
clusters.approach: Ingestion Plane owns execution: add a fill_secret / fill_otp action to Quarry contracts carrying only a secretRef; Quarry resolves it by calling IC /internal/connectors/token or a new IC mailbox-OTP read op with a service token from the cross-plane manifest; BrowserBroker issues a sensitive child grant bound to the origin; Model Plane execution-core raises the approval; the frontend shows an elicitation naming origin and connection. Under ZDR, never persist the value and keep receipts to a boolean.
dependencies: BrowserBroker grant issuance in production (nothing issues grants today)
IC mailbox read op returning a single OTP
clusters.risks: Secret exfiltration via a malicious page or injected iframe if origin checks are weak; phishing pages requesting OTPs; accidental logging in receipts or artifacts; ZDR violations if values persist. Needs prompt-injection defences, which Quarry lacks today.
clusters.rationale: The defining integration-plane overlap gap: both sides exist but never connect, so agents stall at every login/OTP wall. Single source, but the mechanism is SRC-verified and maps onto existing Verevon primitives.

clusters.name: Server-side credential-injecting connector proxy for agents
clusters.description: Users authorise third-party services once; agents call them through a proxy that injects credentials server-side, with per-connector tool restrictions, so credentials never enter agent code.

bestInClass.why: q5 (DOC): MCP connector proxy injects credentials server-side, access ends with the run, per-connector tool allow-lists apply to every Actor; supports OAuth with DCR, a managed client or the user's own OAuth app. Aside (q3 SRC) exposes connectors as REPL globals under one permission model.

clusters.mechanism: A connector record holds OAuth/API-key credentials; the run gets a proxy base URL (ACTOR_MCP_CONNECTOR_BASE_URL) and its input schema declares mcpConnector resources; the proxy authenticates the run, checks the per-connector tool allow-list, injects the credential and forwards; the run's proxy access expires at run end.

evidence: apps/Model Plane/go/services/capability-core/internal/api/registry_apis.go:767 (exact MCP tool allowlist required, max 64)
verevon.gap: Minor: access is scoped per connection/org/user rather than per run (no run-lifetime proxy token); connector actions are a curated static catalog rather than admin-configurable per-connection allow-lists.
verevon.strengths: Equal or ahead: first-party OAuth broker for about 25 providers, encrypted vault, short-lived internal token broker, named whitelisted operations only (raw proxy returns 410), approval-gated writes with signed attestation, exact tool allowlists for MCP servers. Keep the no-raw-proxy rule.

clusters.benefit: Already delivered; per-run scoping would reduce blast radius for long-lived agent runs.
clusters.approach: Optional: bind IC action calls to a run id and expire the capability when the run ends (execution-core passes the run id; IC checks a run-scoped capability token).
clusters.rationale: Verevon is at parity or ahead; keep.

clusters.name: MCP client endpoint hardening (HTTPS-only, no redirects, tool permission rules)
clusters.description: Remote MCP servers and their OAuth endpoints must be HTTPS, redirects are refused, and MCP tools fall under the same tool permission rules.

bestInClass.why: Only source in this set; q3 SRC. Verevon's implementation is stronger (see verevon.strengths).

clusters.mechanism: secureMcpFetch rejects non-HTTPS non-loopback URLs and any 3xx response; permission rules match tool names by mcp__* globs.

evidence: apps/Model Plane/rust/services/model-gateway/src/runtime_registries.rs:426-465 (public HTTPS only, redirect Policy::none, DNS-pinned resolve_to_addrs)
apps/Model Plane/rust/services/model-gateway/src/mcp_oauth.rs:110-163 (server_url, authorization_server, registration and token endpoints must be https; response-supplied hops re-validated)
verevon.strengths: Ahead of Aside: no redirects plus DNS pinning per dial, SSRF re-validation of discovery/DCR/token hops, periodic DNS revalidation with quarantine, a mandatory exact tool allowlist, and mcp__<server>__<tool> namespacing filtered by owner/share. Keep and use as the reference for every new outbound client.

clusters.approach: Keep; reuse the safe_mcp_http_client pattern for Quarry outbound webhooks (see C-t2-10-005).

clusters.name: Chat-app entry points (start agent/browser tasks from Slack, Telegram, Discord)
clusters.description: Users trigger tasks or commands from chat apps via bots or slash commands; results and alerts post back to the channel.

bestInClass.why: Both q3 SRC. Firecrawl's is the cleaner server pattern (OAuth install, signature-verified commands/events, ack-then-async for Slack's 3 s deadline, encrypted bot tokens); Aside covers more channels and treats unpaired senders as untrusted.

clusters.mechanism: OAuth install stores an encrypted bot token per workspace; /commands and /events endpoints verify the Slack signing secret and timestamp, ack within 3 s and enqueue work; replies go via chat.postMessage to a stored channel id. Aside labels channel-origin requests as untrusted context and requires sender pairing.

verevon.gap: No baseline record. Spot check: grep for slash_command/app_mention in integration-corev2/internal and Application Plane/conversation-core found nothing, and Channel Plane is docs-only/future. To check: whether conversation-core or IC treats inbound Slack/Teams messages as agent-task triggers, and whether IC Teams/Slack sync is read-only.
verevon.strengths: IC already has Slack/Discord OAuth, webhook intake with a Rust normaliser, and Teams/Slack message sync.

clusters.benefit: Meets users where they work: starting a governed web-research or monitoring task from Slack is a common request. Low architectural risk if routed through Conversation and Model Plane rather than Quarry.
clusters.approach: Defer to the future Channel Plane. Interim: IC receives signed Slack events (existing webhook intake) and normalises them to a conversation message event; Application Plane conversation-core creates a run via Model Plane; replies go via an IC Slack write action. Treat channel senders as untrusted unless paired with a Verevon identity.
dependencies: Channel Plane design or an interim owner decision
Identity pairing between Slack user and Verevon principal (Control Plane)
clusters.risks: Prompt injection from channel members; identity spoofing; Space ACL widening if channel members are not Verevon principals.
clusters.rationale: Useful, but Channel Plane is explicitly future and this is not core to Quarry/browser parity.

clusters.name: Outbound signed event webhooks for runs and jobs
clusters.description: Run/job lifecycle events (created, succeeded, failed, crawl page, monitor change) POST to customer URLs with signatures, event filters, payload templates and delivery logs; examples include opening GitHub issues on failure.

bestInClass.why: q4 DOC: richest event vocabulary (RUN/BUILD lifecycle incl. timed-out and resurrected), payload and header templates, ad-hoc per-run webhooks. Firecrawl (q3 SRC) adds SSRF refusal of private targets, wildcard event filters and delivery logs, but has a single attempt without retry.

clusters.mechanism: Webhook {url, secret, eventTypes[], payloadTemplate, headersTemplate, org scope}; on an event, render the template with {{eventType, eventData, resource, createdAt}}; sign the body with timestamped HMAC-SHA256; deliver through an SSRF-guarded client (no private IPs, DNS pinning, no redirects); retry with backoff into a DLQ; log each attempt for the tenant.

evidence: apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/services/quarry-control/internal/dispatcher/dispatcher.go:36-41 and cmd/control/main.go:197 (plain http.Client passed as nil, no SSRF guard seen; INF from code)
apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/services/quarry-control/internal/store/store.go:376-383 (Webhook has an Events filter but no org_id)
verevon.gap: Delivery engine beats Firecrawl (retries, DLQ, timestamped signature), but webhooks are not tenant-scoped, not exposed via edge, have no per-job ad-hoc webhook and no payload/header templates, and the dispatcher uses a plain HTTP client with no private-address/redirect guard (must be fixed before tenant-registered URLs are allowed). No customer-facing IC run/sync lifecycle webhooks. Baseline narrative v-quarry section 1 covers this; no category-10 baseline record.
verevon.strengths: Retry/backoff/DLQ and timestamped HMAC signatures are ahead of Firecrawl.

clusters.benefit: Lets customers and Verevon's own Application Plane react to crawl/agent run completion without polling; required for Firecrawl/Apify async-job parity.
clusters.approach: Add org_id to webhooks and deliveries; front CRUD through quarry-edge with JWT org scoping; add a per-request webhook field on crawl/batch/agent runs; port the Model Plane safe_mcp_http_client rules (HTTPS, DNS pin, no redirects, forbidden ranges) into the Go dispatcher; add a delivery-log listing; send ids only (no payload content) under ZDR.
clusters.risks: SSRF to internal services if the guard is missing; data leakage in payloads under ZDR; secret rotation.
clusters.rationale: The engine exists; tenant scoping plus an SSRF guard is moderate work with high parity value.

clusters.name: No-code automation platform apps and API chaining
clusters.description: Official Make, Zapier, n8n and Gumloop apps start runs and consume results; API clients chain runs (call, wait, read dataset).
clusters.mechanism: Published connector apps per platform wrap the REST API (start run, poll/wait, fetch dataset items), plus an SDK call() helper that blocks until the run finishes.

evidence: apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/sdks/typescript/src/apis (OpenAPI-generated TS client; a Python client also exists, per v-quarry baseline section 1)
verevon.gap: No baseline record. Quarry has OpenAPI TS/Python SDKs; no Zapier/Make/n8n apps were looked for. To check: any Zapier/n8n artefacts in the repo, and whether the SDK offers a call-and-wait helper.
verevon.strengths: OpenAPI SDKs are a base for chaining.

clusters.benefit: Limited for an AI-first product whose own agents orchestrate work; mainly a go-to-market channel.
clusters.approach: If pursued, publish an n8n node first (open source, self-hostable) over the edge API; no plane changes.
dependencies: Stable public async job lifecycle and webhooks (C-t2-10-005)
clusters.risks: API surface lock-in before Quarry request shapes stabilise.
clusters.rationale: Supported only by DOC records from a single platform benchmark; not on the critical path.

clusters.name: Quarry and connectors exposed to external agents (MCP server, framework wrappers, coding-agent plugins) with audience-bound auth
clusters.description: Scraping, browser and provider capabilities are published as an MCP server and as tools for LangChain, OpenAI Agents SDK, CrewAI and coding agents, authenticated with audience-bound OAuth tokens or short-lived delegated credentials.

bestInClass.why: q4 SRC with concrete auth: OAuth tokens introspected (active, exp, aud bound to the API or MCP resource, credential_purpose), a cache keyed by token hash with outage isolation, WWW-Authenticate protected-resource metadata; a delegated fcmcp_ HMAC credential with a strict key set, purpose and clock-skew limits. Apify (q4 DOC) has the widest distribution (one-command install into about 12 coding agents, framework wrappers).

clusters.mechanism: The hosted MCP service authenticates the client via OAuth (protected-resource metadata advertised in WWW-Authenticate); it introspects the token at the auth server and requires aud == MCP resource and purpose hosted_mcp_oauth. To call the core API it mints a short-lived signed credential {v, aud core, purpose, subject key, iat, exp} (exp <= 120 s, iat skew <= 30 s) verified with a constant-time HMAC; no user token is forwarded.

evidence: apps/Ingestion Plane/Quarry-v2/docs/OSS_PARITY_BACKLOG.md section 2 (MCP explicitly deferred as Skip)
verevon.gap: No MCP server, CLI, skills or framework wrappers for Quarry or IC, and no audience-bound OAuth introspection for external agent clients. Verevon consumes MCP but does not expose it.
verevon.strengths: The cross-plane service-token manifest and Quarry service-principal route scoping are a base for purpose-tagged delegation.

clusters.benefit: Lets customers' own agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) use Verevon's governed web layer and connectors with ZDR and audit intact, giving parity with Firecrawl/Apify developer experience.
clusters.approach: Build an MCP front in the Frontend Plane gateway (Rust) or a dedicated edge service: OAuth via Control Plane auth-core with resource indicators (aud = verevon-mcp) and introspection cached by token hash; translate calls to Quarry edge and IC with a short-lived purpose-tagged service token from the cross-plane manifest; the tool set mirrors execution-core tools (search, scrape, extract, provider actions read-only by default; writes require in-product approval).
dependencies: Control Plane OAuth authorization server with resource indicators
clusters.risks: Bypassing Model Plane approvals if writes are exposed; quota abuse; ZDR propagation to external clients; token replay across resources if aud is not enforced.
clusters.rationale: High ecosystem value and parity with both web benchmarks, but it does not block Verevon's in-product vision; do it after the connector-browser bridge and grant issuance.

clusters.name: Per-tool-call audit logs for externally invoked tools (privacy-minimised, ZDR-aware)
clusters.description: Each external MCP tool call writes a log row (tool, client, auth type, status, error class, request id) visible to the team without exposing intent fields; ZDR short-circuits storage.

bestInClass.why: Only source; q4 SRC with constant-time shared-secret ingest, 64 KB body cap, rate limit, actor validation, a cursor-paged team view with objective and job id deliberately excluded, and ZDR returning 202 without storing.

clusters.mechanism: The MCP service POSTs one row per call to an internal ingest endpoint; rows go to a columnar store with a retention window; the team GET lists rows with cursor pagination over a reduced column set; ZDR teams get a 202 disposition and nothing is stored.

evidence: apps/Ingestion Plane/integration-corev2/internal/api/audit_outbox.go:46-48 (durable audit outbox to Audit Core for connection.action.* events)
apps/Model Plane/rust/services/model-gateway/src/audit.rs:1-22 (Session Core reserve-before-execute/finalize audit outbox; MCP tools classed 'unclassified')
verevon.gap: Internal audit of provider actions and tool calls exists, but there is no external MCP front to audit, MCP tool calls get data category 'unclassified', and no team-readable, privacy-minimised tool-call log view was found (Audit Core not checked).
verevon.strengths: A transactional audit outbox to Audit Core is stronger than a best-effort ingest endpoint.

clusters.benefit: Required companion to C-t2-10-007; also improves admin visibility of agent MCP usage today.
clusters.approach: Classify MCP tool data categories at registration (capability-core) instead of 'unclassified'; expose an Audit Core query view filtered to tool-call events with intent fields omitted; under ZDR record only metadata.
clusters.risks: Logging prompts or arguments would leak intent and break ZDR.
clusters.rationale: Foundations exist; it only matters once tools are exposed externally.

clusters.name: Provider capability discovery by domain or intent
clusters.description: Search or scrape returns provider tools matched to the page's domain or the query (for example a GitHub URL suggests GitHub actions) with contracts and price; one execution endpoint runs any discovered capability.

bestInClass.why: q4; 103 is SRC (scrapeController diverts alexandria bodies, discoverTools limit 24 with a 10 s budget, refused under ZDR, compact|summary|full detail levels); 099 is DOC from the service README.

clusters.mechanism: Catalog entries {provider, capability, description, inputSchema, price, domains[]}; discovery matches by domain (URL host -> provider) or semantic search over descriptions; the response returns data.tools with matchedBy domain|semantic and matchedUrls; execution is one endpoint taking [{provider, capability, options}] with a caller request id; discovery is disabled under ZDR because it calls an external exchange.

evidence: apps/Model Plane/rust/services/execution-core/src/integration_tools.rs:60-75 (hard-coded curated CATALOG of operations with summaries)
verevon.gap: The agent sees a static curated operation list (list_provider_actions) for connections it already has; no domain-to-provider matching from browsed URLs, no input schemas in an IC-served catalog, and no suggestion to connect a provider when the agent browses its site.
verevon.strengths: A single named-operation execution surface with write approvals already exists; IC per-connection capability/discovery routes are a base.

clusters.benefit: When the agent browses github.com or a Shopify admin it can switch to a governed API action instead of brittle UI clicking: faster, cheaper, auditable, and fewer sensitive browser grants. Directly reduces Quarry load and risk.
clusters.approach: IC serves a versioned capability catalog (operation, schema, isWrite, provider domains) generated from the Execute switch; execution-core loads it instead of the static CATALOG; Quarry observations include the canonical host; Model Plane matches host to catalog and offers matching actions (or a connect suggestion) in the next step. Keep discovery internal (no external exchange) so ZDR is unaffected.
dependencies: Model Plane tool-selection budget (avoid tool flooding)
clusters.risks: Tool-list bloat degrading model selection (the CATALOG comment warns of this); stale domain mappings.
clusters.rationale: Unique to Firecrawl but a strong fit for Verevon's architecture; ties browser and connectors together at low risk.

clusters.name: Idempotent, receipted (and metered) provider action execution
clusters.description: Provider calls are authorised, priced, reserved, executed, settled and ledgered; a request id makes replays safe, payload changes conflict, and uncertain outcomes are held for reconciliation.

bestInClass.why: q4 SRC design: charge id sha256(team, request id), 7-day record with states completed (replay), different payload (409), in flight (409), refused (dropped), unresolved (503 kept for manual reconciliation); credit lock and finalise. Settlement is tested only with mocks.

clusters.mechanism: Derive a deterministic id from tenant and caller request id; store the record before execution; on retry compare the payload hash; reserve credits with a lock id, execute with a deadline, finalise the receipt and enqueue ledger and usage events; unknown outcomes are never retried automatically.

evidence: apps/Ingestion Plane/integration-corev2/internal/api/server.go:3093-3120 (idempotency key required for write actions)
verevon.gap: No per-action price quote or credit reservation for paid provider calls (billing is usage-metered elsewhere); read actions are not idempotency-tracked (acceptable).
verevon.strengths: Ahead: mandatory idempotency keys on writes, request-hash conflict detection, signed attestation of the acting user, receipt states including unknown, all inside an audit transaction drained to Audit Core. Keep.

clusters.approach: Only if paid provider actions appear: add quote/reserve via Control Plane billing before execute.
clusters.rationale: Verevon is at parity or ahead on the guarantees that matter.

clusters.name: Scraped and synced data into knowledge stores and destinations
clusters.description: Results flow into knowledge/vector stores, warehouses, drives and CRMs, or into an index that serves cached scrapes.

bestInClass.why: q4 DOC breadth: Snowflake, Airtable, Google Drive, HubSpot, Pinecone/Qdrant/OpenAI vector stores with incremental updates. Firecrawl (q3 SRC) feeds a cross-tenant shared index, which Verevon must not copy.

clusters.mechanism: Integration jobs read a run's dataset and upsert into the destination with incremental keys; Firecrawl samples documents to a RabbitMQ indexer that writes object storage plus an index DB row keyed by URL hash for maxAge cache hits.

verevon.gap: Into Verevon's own Data Plane: shipped (IC handoff; Quarry ingest via the Data Plane contract per v-quarry baseline section 6). External destinations (warehouses, external vector DBs) are absent, which is acceptable for a knowledge-owning product; IC write actions (Drive, Sheets) can cover user-driven exports.
verevon.strengths: Tenant-isolated ingest through the Data Plane contract respects ZDR and the no-cross-plane-DB rule; do not adopt a cross-tenant shared scrape cache.

clusters.approach: Keep; if export demand appears, expose 'export dataset to Drive/Sheets' as IC write actions.
clusters.risks: Cross-tenant caching would violate ZDR and ACL rules.
clusters.rationale: Verevon's design is deliberately different and sound.

clusters.name: Alert notification destinations with recipient consent (Slack channel, double opt-in email, unsubscribe)
clusters.description: Monitor alerts go to a webhook, Slack or up to 25 email recipients; external recipients stay pending until they confirm, and each has an unsubscribe token.

bestInClass.why: Only source; q4 SRC: recipient table with pending|confirmed|unsubscribed, 256-bit tokens, public token-only confirm/unsubscribe routes, includeDiffs toggle.

clusters.mechanism: Recipient rows with status and random tokens; a confirmation email on add; only confirmed recipients receive alerts; an unsubscribe link flips status; diff embedding is optional.

verevon.gap: notification-core delivers to org members over in_app/email/sms/push with delivery-state tracking; no Slack channel destination and no external-recipient double opt-in/unsubscribe were found (spot check, not exhaustive). Quarry change events reach notification-core (v-quarry baseline section 1).
verevon.strengths: Callback-confirmed delivery states and org-level channel configuration.

clusters.benefit: Lets change-monitor alerts reach Slack and external stakeholders compliantly.
clusters.approach: Add a Slack destination in notification-core that calls an IC Slack write action (no tokens held in notification-core); add opt-in/unsubscribe only if non-member recipients are allowed.
clusters.risks: Spam/compliance issues if external recipients are added without opt-in; ZDR (no diffs in email).
clusters.rationale: Small polish for change monitoring; not core.

clusters.name: Partner/user provisioning API
clusters.description: An admin surface lets an integration partner create users and validate or rotate API keys.

bestInClass.why: Only source; q2 SRC and weak (secret embedded in the URL path).

clusters.mechanism: Path-secret-gated admin routes proxied to an integrations service with an S2S secret.

verevon.gap: None relevant; partner key rotation belongs to Control Plane.
verevon.strengths: Standards-based SCIM with Control Plane principals is better; never adopt a secret-in-path admin gate.

clusters.name: Automatic sign-in of embedded first-party views (short-lived token, account and residency routing)
clusters.description: Opening first-party hosted sites or embedded product pages in the in-app browser signs the user in via a short-lived token on the first navigation and routes to the right account and data-residency region.

bestInClass.why: q4 SRC: host-suffix allowlist, 3 s bootstrap budget, token lifetime capped at 120 s, header sent only on that navigation and aborted if superseded; account/residency cookies set and cleared with the guest; navigation off first-party blocked.

clusters.mechanism: For https first-party hosts (no port, no userinfo) POST session_bootstrap {target_url} -> {id_token, expires_in<=120}; load the page with a one-shot header. For embedded app views, validate the account match, set routing cookies (account, residency region, fedramp), clear them when the guest is destroyed, and block external navigation.

verevon.gap: No baseline record. To check: whether the remote Quarry browser ever opens Verevon-hosted previews (Studio/app previews) and how auth is done there; whether org residency from Control Plane propagates into Quarry session placement.

clusters.benefit: Removes sign-in friction for Verevon-hosted previews inside the remote browser and makes sure residency is honoured in browser sessions.
clusters.approach: The gateway mints a short-lived, audience-bound preview token (Control Plane) passed to Quarry as a one-shot navigation header for allowlisted first-party hosts; never expose it to the model or the SPA.
clusters.risks: Token leakage to third-party frames; header replay.
clusters.rationale: Only valuable once Verevon hosts previews that users open in the browser.

clusters.name: Sandboxed, agent-operable rendering of integration/MCP App UIs
clusters.description: Interactive UI returned by tools or MCP servers renders in a locked-down sandbox origin with request, navigation and permission blocking, and the agent can operate it with locators.

bestInClass.why: Only source; q4 SRC: dedicated sandbox host and scheme, only about/blob/data/https/wss allowed, attach requests queued with expiry, agent backend limited to locator actions.

clusters.mechanism: Render MCP App resources in a guest view on a separate sandbox origin; a session request filter allows only safe schemes; permission requests are denied; the agent drives the view through accessibility locators, never raw script.

evidence: apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/chat/components/ChatArtifactPanel.tsx:503-518 (artifacts in iframe sandbox=allow-scripts without allow-same-origin)
apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/dashboard/home/DashboardSearchResults.tsx:184 (iframe with allow-scripts plus allow-same-origin; worth a review)
verevon.gap: Chat artifacts are sandboxed, but no MCP Apps (ui:// resource) rendering was found and the agent cannot operate rendered widgets. Spot check only.
verevon.strengths: Opaque-origin artifact iframes are the right default.

clusters.benefit: Lets integration results (forms, pickers, dashboards from MCP servers) appear inline and be operated safely by the user or the agent.
clusters.approach: Frontend Plane renders MCP App resources in an opaque-origin iframe served from a separate sandbox domain with a CSP; a postMessage bridge proxies tool calls through the gateway to Model Plane approvals.
dependencies: Model Plane MCP gateway support for UI resources
clusters.risks: Sandbox escape when allow-scripts and allow-same-origin are combined on same-origin content; phishing UI inside widgets.
clusters.rationale: Emerging capability; not a parity blocker.

clusters.name: Signed host-to-runtime tool responses over an authenticated local pipe
clusters.description: The desktop host exposes tools and browser access to the local executor over a peer-authorised pipe and signs each response so the executor can trust it.

bestInClass.why: Only source; q4 SRC: per-process Ed25519 key, verifying identity handed to the REPL, socket peer authorizer, methods tools/list|call|cancel and browser/access.

clusters.mechanism: The host generates an Ed25519 key per process, passes the SPKI public key to the runtime, and returns {payload, signature} for every tool response; the runtime verifies before acting.

verevon.gap: No baseline record. Verevon's agent runtime is server-side; browser authority is BrowserBroker grants and IC writes use signed attestations. To check: whether Model Plane sandboxes call back to host tools and how those responses are authenticated.
verevon.strengths: Signed write attestations in IC already apply the same idea where it matters.

clusters.benefit: Low today; relevant only if a local/desktop executor or a sandbox callback path is added.
clusters.approach: If needed, sign sandbox-manager tool responses with a per-lease key.
clusters.rationale: Solves a desktop local-executor trust problem that Verevon does not have.

clusters.name: Control of the user's own browser via extension and native messaging host
clusters.description: The agent drives the user's own Chrome/Edge/Brave profile through an extension and a native host bridged to the app server, with version negotiation and extension-id allowlisting.

bestInClass.why: Only source; q4 SRC: Rust native host, allowed-origin check, manifest schema with required protocol versions and explicit update-required errors, size-bounded chunked tab-context transfer.

clusters.mechanism: Extension <-> native host over stdin/stdout; native host <-> app server over a local WebSocket/named pipe; the manifest pins extension ids and protocol versions; tab-context assets are written in bounded chunks.

evidence: findings/t2/v-browser-app.baseline.md section 7 (extensions absent; grep over browser feature files)
CLAUDE.md gateway rule: the browser never sees CDP endpoints, Quarry tokens or provider secrets
verevon.gap: No extension or native host; all browsing is a remote leased Chromium in Quarry.
verevon.strengths: A remote isolated browser keeps ZDR, egress control and grants enforceable server-side.

clusters.benefit: Access to sites where the user is already logged in, without re-authentication; an alternative path to authenticated web that competes with C-t2-10-001.
clusters.approach: If pursued, a Verevon extension that relays proposals from Model Plane and executes locally under grant checks; egress proof, ZDR and receipts would be weaker than in Quarry.
clusters.risks: Breaks the server-side containment model, exposes the user's full profile to agent actions, is hard to audit, and conflicts with 'Quarry executes'.
clusters.rationale: Users would value it, but the connector-to-browser bridge delivers most of the benefit inside the governed architecture first.

clusters.name: Tab and browser mention references in prompts
clusters.description: Prompts can reference an exact browser tab via a deep-link scheme carrying browser id, tab id, title and url, which the agent must resolve and validate.

bestInClass.why: Only source; q3 DOC (bundled plugin docs, not code-verified).

clusters.mechanism: plugin://browser@...?mention=tab-v1&browserId&tabId&title&url; the resolver selects the matching browser/profile and validates the snapshot title/url against the live tab.

verevon.gap: No baseline record. On a spot check the SpacePage mention list covers Space tabs (verevonv3/src/features/spaces/components/SpacePage.tsx:119), not browser sessions. To check: whether the chat composer can reference a live browser session/tab.

clusters.benefit: Lets users point the agent at the exact page they are viewing; a small UX win.
clusters.approach: Define a verevon://browser-session/<id>/tab/<id>?title&url mention token in the composer; Model Plane resolves it via a Quarry session ownership check (org + actor).
clusters.risks: Referencing another actor's session would widen the ACL; ownership must be checked.
clusters.rationale: Supported only by a DOC record from a single source; small benefit.

clusters.name: Native password-manager bridge (Apple Passwords)
clusters.description: Read and save credentials in the OS password manager through a native host using a PIN-paired PAKE handshake and an encrypted channel.

bestInClass.why: Only source; q3 SRC: SRP-like handshake with a user-visible PIN, AES-GCM session channel.

clusters.mechanism: connectNative to the password manager host; capabilities, PAKE hello, then AES-GCM encrypted messages under a derived key; the user confirms the PIN.

verevon.gap: No password manager or autofill integration; the remote browser cannot reach a local OS keychain.

clusters.benefit: Minimal for a remote, server-side browser.
clusters.approach: Do not build; cover credentials through the connector/vault secretRef path (C-t2-10-001).
clusters.risks: Local keychain access is incompatible with remote execution and ZDR.
clusters.rationale: Desktop/macOS-specific; does not fit Verevon's remote browser architecture.
